images.caption: In the southwest wall, the wooden fixtures are heavily weathered, they seem to be over 100 years old. The small chapel at the foot of the rock face is dedicated to the Panagia.

images.caption: In the southwest wall of the Bandova stone, according to the information in the available books, the facility was destroyed by a bomb hit in 1943 and would be unused since then. Apparently, it was rebuilt after all. Like the monastery of Ágios Andónios, located in the immediate vicinity, the monastery is not open to the public. Both are not noticed by most visitors despite their location between Kalambáka and Kastráki.Whether the cableway at the bottom right is used only for material transport or represents the only access is not apparent.
